standard.name: Independent Poisson innovations and independent Bernoulli thinning trials
Independent sampling from the observational count law

definitions.name: Strict causally sufficient Poisson branching model class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_d^\circ=\{(G,\mu,\alpha,P):G\text{ is a DAG on }V,\ \mu\in(0,\infty)^V,\ \alpha\in(0,1)^{E(G)},\ P=\mathcal L(X),\ \text{ass:structural-recursion and ass:independent-branching-law hold}\}\)

definitions.name: Repeated-label genealogy weights
definitions.construction: \(\Gamma_i(k)=\{\gamma:\gamma\text{ is a finite open-edge descendant genealogy rooted at }i\text{ with observed-label multiplicity }k\},\quad w_\gamma=\prod_{e\in O_1(\gamma)}\alpha_e\prod_{e\in O_0(\gamma)}(1-\alpha_e)\)

definitions.name: Compelled incoming arrows and residual graph
definitions.construction: \(A(P)=\{i\to k:\exists j\in V,\ \mathsf{Head}_P(i,j;k)\},\quad M(P)=\{k:\exists i,j\in V,\ \mathsf{Head}_P(i,j;k)\},\quad F(P)=S(P)\setminus\{\{i,k\}:i\to k\in A(P)\}\)

definitions.name: Strict degree-three collision witness
definitions.construction: \(\mu_s=6,\ \mu_m=2,\ \mu_r=1,\ \alpha_{sm}=2/3,\ \alpha_{sr}=1/2,\ \alpha_{mr}=1/2\) on \(s\to m\to r\) and \(s\to r\), for each choice of sink \(r\) among three labels

definitions.name: Simultaneous coefficient confidence region
definitions.construction: \(\epsilon_n=\sqrt{\log(2|I_4|/\eta)/(2n)},\quad Q_n=\{q:q_x\ge0,\ \sum_{x\in I_4}q_x\le1,\ q_0>0,\ |q_x-\widehat p_x|\le\epsilon_n\ (x\in I_4)\},\quad C_n=\{T(q):q\in Q_n\}\)

definitions.name: Certified source-forest outward-inversion handle
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf A_{\mathrm{out}}\): combine interval screening of singleton, pair, and degree-four head coordinates with source-forest component enumeration, reverse-topological interval decoding, and certificate-preserving branch-and-bound for the target set \(\mathcal D_n\)

statements.statement: For every \((G,\mu,\alpha,P)\in\mathcal M_d^\circ\) and every nonzero multi-index \(k\), the exact-support coefficient satisfies \(c_k=\sum_{i\in V}\mu_i\sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma_i(k)}w_\gamma\). The identity counts genealogical occurrences before observed labels are merged, so distinct downstream paths that repeat a vertex label contribute to the same exponent without cancellation.
statements.justification: This is the load-bearing bridge from arbitrary-DAG branching genealogies to every local coefficient certificate.
statements.gap: Xiang et al. give a path-to-monomial correspondence, but the repeated-label multiplicity bookkeeping needed for a universal low-degree converse is not isolated in their Proposition 1.
statements.consumer: The source-forest converse and the degree-four compression theorem both use this formula to rule out false signatures from overlapping descendants.

statements.statement: For every strict-model law \(P\), \(c_{e_i+e_j}>0\) if and only if \(\{i,j\}\in S(P)\). On every induced path \(i-k-j\), \(c_{e_i+e_j+e_k}=0\) if and only if \(i\to k\leftarrow j\). On every triangle, \(c_{e_i+e_j+2e_k}>0\) if and only if \(i\to k\leftarrow j\). Consequently \(A(P)\) is exactly the union of all arrows entering every vertex of indegree at least two in every member of \(\mathcal D(P)\).
statements.justification: The theorem converts degree-four observable coordinates into the complete set of fixed incoming arrows.
statements.gap: Xiang et al. establish the local tests, while the claim here assembles them over every parent pair without faithfulness and makes their fiber-wide invariance explicit.
statements.consumer: The residual-forest theorem uses \(A(P)\) as its observable anchor set.

statements.statement: If \(u\) is a source of \(G\), \(\operatorname{Pa}_G(v)=\{u\}\), and \(u\to v\in E\), then \(\mathsf R_{u\to v}\) is acyclic, all transformed rates and thinning probabilities are strict, and its complete log-PGF equals \(\Psi_P\) identically, including the constant coefficient. The equality remains valid when \(u\) and \(v\) have arbitrarily overlapping descendant sets.
statements.justification: This transformation supplies a positive same-law witness for every admissible ambiguity.
statements.gap: Qiao et al. give the two-variable reverse representation; they do not prove a complete-PGF identity inside an arbitrary graph with shared descendants.
statements.consumer: Every free-tree rerooting in the complete fiber obtains an explicit alternative mechanism and parameter point.

statements.statement: For any \(G\in\mathcal D(P)\), the reverse-topological recursion in \(\theta_G(P)\) returns the unique \((\mu,\alpha)\in(0,\infty)^V\times(0,1)^{E(G)}\) inducing \(P\). Every denominator is positive, and the fixed-DAG coefficient map has full column rank throughout the strict parameter domain.
statements.justification: Graph ambiguity is separated cleanly from numerical nonidentification by a constructive inverse.
statements.gap: Xiang et al. estimate PGF statistics for graph learning but do not state a global fixed-DAG rational inverse or parameter-fiber injectivity theorem.
statements.consumer: Analysts can decode and compare every mechanism in the football-event and shopping-mall observational fibers.

statements.statement: For every \(P\) generated by \(\mathcal M_d^\circ\), \(F(P)\) is a forest, each connected component of \(F(P)\) contains at most one vertex of \(M(P)\), and \(\mathcal D(P)=\{G_\rho:\rho(T)\in T\text{ for every }T\in\mathcal T_0(P)\}\). A component meeting \(M(P)\) is directed away from its unique anchor, and each free component is independently directed away from its chosen root. This necessary-and-sufficient classification strictly strengthens the sufficient local orientation conclusions of Xiang et al. and Qiao et al.
statements.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: the complete one-law observational equivalence class is an explicit source-forest root-choice family.
statements.gap: Qiao et al. and Xiang et al. give sufficient path or local PGF orientations, but neither paper proves an arbitrary-DAG converse or exhausts every compatible representation.
statements.consumer: The result turns the remaining unoriented football and shopping arrows into certified ambiguity classes instead of unresolved algorithm output.

statements.statement: The exact fiber size is \(|\mathcal D(P)|=\prod_{T\in\mathcal T_0(P)}|T|\). An edge is compelled if and only if it does not lie in a free tree; its certificate is either a local head signature or the unique path from an anchor. Every free-tree edge admits both directions, certified by a finite sequence of maps \(\mathsf R_{u\to v}\).
statements.justification: Cardinality and certificates make the equivalence theorem directly auditable at the edge level.
statements.gap: No cited PB-SCM paper counts the full fiber or supplies constructive certificates for both compelled and reversible arrows.
statements.consumer: Applied users can report which event pathways are invariant across all mechanisms and enumerate every admissible alternative.

statements.statement: For any two laws \(P,P'\) generated by \(\mathcal M_d^\circ\), \(t_4(P)=t_4(P')\) if and only if \(P=P'\). Equality of \(t_4\) also implies \(\mathcal D(P)=\mathcal D(P')\) and \(\theta_G(P)=\theta_G(P')\) for every compatible \(G\).
statements.justification: A fixed low-order signature determines an arbitrarily high-degree branching law and its entire graph-parameter fiber.
statements.gap: Qiao et al. use a path-dependent cumulant order and Xiang et al. use the complete PGF; neither gives a universal finite cutoff.
statements.consumer: The full population identification problem reduces to finitely many count-cell functionals for any fixed number of vertices.

statements.statement: The three strict triangle laws in the construction \(\text{def:triangle-witness}\) have identical \(\Psi_P(0)\) and identical \(c_k\) for every \(|k|\le3\), but their coefficients of \(z_s z_m z_r^2\) differ and their DAG fibers have different triangle sinks. Adding independent positive-Poisson coordinates extends the failure to every \(d\ge3\).
statements.justification: The explicit strict witness proves that degree four is minimal rather than merely sufficient.
statements.gap: The cited PB-SCM papers exhibit direction asymmetry but do not provide two strict laws agreeing through every degree-three log-PGF coordinate.
statements.consumer: Any PGF procedure claiming universal recovery can be tested against the precise fourth-degree obstruction.

statements.statement: For every distribution \(P\) on \(\mathbb N_0^V\) with \(p_0>0\), \(T_k((p_x)_{x\in I_4})=c_k\) for \(1\le|k|\le4\), and \(\Pr_P\{t_4(P)\in C_n\}\ge1-\eta\). The inequality is finite-sample and uniform over \(\mathcal M_d^\circ\), without a lower bound on \(p_0\).
statements.justification: The finite rational log-series identity converts bounded cell concentration into honest simultaneous coefficient coverage.
statements.gap: Xiang et al. use bootstrap rank tests and Nakamura and Perez-Abreu study empirical-PGF inference, but neither constructs this denominator-safe finite coefficient region.
statements.consumer: The coefficient region is the input for graph-set inference in sparse football and shopping count tables.

statements.statement: The outward inverse satisfies \(\Pr_P\{\mathcal D(P)\subseteq\mathcal D_n\}\ge1-\eta\) uniformly over \(\mathcal M_d^\circ\). Conditional on \(\mathcal D_n\ne\varnothing\), reporting only arrows present with the same orientation in every \(G\in\mathcal D_n\) controls the probability of any false compulsion by \(\eta\).
statements.justification: Inference targets the full non-singleton population fiber and therefore avoids false certainty from graph-then-report workflows.
statements.gap: Strieder et al. invert tests for linear-model effects and Wang et al. give asymptotic ordering sets; neither covers every graph in a strict PB-SCM population fiber with finite-sample probability.
statements.consumer: The football-event and shopping-mall analyses can report only causal arrows supported simultaneously across structural and sampling uncertainty.

statements.statement: Can \(\mathsf A_{\mathrm{out}}\) be constructed so that, for rational empirical cell frequencies and rational \(\eta\), it returns exactly \(\mathcal D_n\), emits a valid inclusion or exclusion certificate for every labeled DAG, terminates with delay polynomial in the input bit length and \(d\) between successive output source-forest classes, and preserves the coverage conclusion of \(\text{thm:outer-fiber-confidence}\)?
statements.justification: The population geometry suggests an exact output-sensitive alternative to generic semialgebraic elimination, but its complexity is genuinely open.
statements.gap: Existing causal-model inversion papers do not exploit a source-forest quotient, and the PB-SCM papers provide point algorithms rather than certified outward enumeration.
statements.consumer: A positive answer would make honest full-fiber confidence reporting computationally usable beyond very small event systems.

sampling_model.design: Independent observational sampling from one strict Poisson branching SCM law.
sampling_model.units: The units are \(n\) independent realizations of the complete labeled count vector \(X\).
sampling_model.treatment: There is no designated treatment; the structural target is the labeled DAG fiber.
sampling_model.overlap: No faithfulness, edge-strength margin, compact parameter box, or positive lower bound on \(p_0\) is imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The low-count probabilities \(p_x\), \(x\in I_4\), are estimated by bounded cell indicators and mapped outward through \(T(q)\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 4--7 recover the skeleton and give local PGF conditions sufficient to orient triangle sinks, unshielded colliders, and arrows entering a vertex with another parent.
Remark 1 gives a distributionally equivalent reverse model for every two-variable PB-SCM, while Theorems 6--7 give path-cumulant conditions sufficient for some causal directions.
Theorem 1 characterizes graph-level distribution equivalence in linear Gaussian directed graphs by support rotations and column swaps.
Theorem 14 identifies a binomial-thinning DAG when every nonsink innovation is non-Poisson, while the all-Poisson PB-SCM is exceptional.
Theorem 1 obtains an asymptotic confidence set for a total causal effect by inverting model-aware tests in a bivariate homoscedastic linear SEM.
The ordering-set procedure has asymptotic coverage for at least one valid causal ordering and supports post-processing into ancestral-relation envelopes.
The empirical probability-generating-function goodness-of-fit statistic has a derived limiting distribution under a Poisson null.

tldr: Event-count branching models encode causal structure beyond conditional independence, yet their strict all-Poisson form admits genuine direction reversals. The proposal characterizes the complete one-law observational fiber. Degree-four exact-support log-PGF coefficients recover the skeleton and every arrow entering a multi-parent vertex; deleting those arrows leaves anchored and free trees, and the fiber consists exactly of independently rerooting the free trees. A positive source-edge reversal realizes every alternative, while a reverse-topological rational decoder yields the unique parameter point on each graph. Degree four determines the entire strict-model law and is minimal by an explicit triangle collision through degree three. A bounded-cell confidence region is outward-inverted to cover the whole population fiber, and only arrows unanimous over a nonempty outer set are reported.

project_justification.gap: Published PB-SCM theory supplies path-based or local PGF orientation criteria but no necessary-and-sufficient description of every DAG and parameter point generating a fixed strict all-Poisson observational law.
project_justification.niche: The local parent-pair signatures leave a structured residual ambiguity that can be classified globally without faithfulness and can be carried into honest set-valued inference.
project_justification.fill: The source-forest theorem gives the exact fiber, transformations, cardinality, certificates, and rational inverse; the sharp degree-four theorem compresses the full PGF; and outward coefficient inversion provides finite-sample coverage of the unrestricted fiber.

related_work: Qiao et al. (2024) connect arbitrary-order cumulants to directed-path multiplicity, establish sufficient orientation conditions, and give the bivariate reversal that motivates the source-edge transformation. Xiang et al. (2024) derive the recursive PB-SCM PGF and local skeleton, triangle, and collider signatures; their event-count framing and football and shopping applications are the direct empirical motivation, while their global observational fiber remains unstated. Ghassami et al. (2020) separate distribution equivalence from conditional-independence equivalence in linear Gaussian directed graphs and provide a methodological template for explicit same-law transformations, but their algebra and equivalence target differ. Gao, Cai, and Hara (2026) show that the all-Poisson PB-SCM is exceptional and obtain full identification after changing the thinning or nonsink innovation model; they do not characterize the exceptional model's fiber. Qiao et al. (2026) address local three-variable monomial equivalence under latent confounding, a different model and scope. Strieder et al. (2021) and Wang, Kolar, and Drton (2026) show how inversion and relation envelopes retain causal-structure uncertainty, but their guarantees concern restricted linear or additive-error models rather than finite-sample coverage of a non-singleton PB-SCM population fiber. Nakamura and Perez-Abreu (1993) provide classical empirical-PGF inference; the present low-degree rational cell map specializes that idea to structural-fiber coverage.
technical_internal_limitation: The strict interior is essential. At zero thinning an edge is observationally absent, at zero innovation a source can disappear, and at deterministic thinning the positive failure patterns and decoder denominators can fail. The coefficient confidence region may be unbounded when the data do not bound \(p_0\) away from zero. These facts preclude automatic uniform singleton recovery on the unrestricted class and are not repaired by imposing an undeclared compact parameter box.
honest_scope: The formal claims concern finite labeled causally sufficient DAGs, independent positive Poisson innovations, and edge probabilities strictly between zero and one. As a required sanity reduction, when \(d=2\) and one edge is present, the source-forest theorem yields exactly the two orientations and the transformation in Qiao et al.; when the skeleton is empty, it yields the unique empty DAG. No automatic faithfulness theorem, latent-confounded extension, boundary-fiber theorem, numerical stability bound, or unrestricted uniform singleton-consistency result is claimed. The arbitrary-DAG repeated-label genealogy lemma is the central proof obligation. Exact polynomial-delay outward inversion is posed as an open-ended question rather than asserted.

seed_details.title: Complete source-forest observational fiber
seed_details.anchor_opened: Introduction, Theorems 1--2 and their recursive PGF proof, Proposition 1, Theorems 4--7 and their proofs, Section 5.2, and Conclusion were read in the NeurIPS paper.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The published argument maps PGF components to local patterns and gives sufficient orientations; the first new step is to aggregate every detected parent pair, delete the resulting incoming arrows, and prove that the residual graph is a forest with exactly one admissible root per anchored component.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Xiang et al. because Theorem 7 already orients every arrow entering a vertex that has another parent.
seed_details.rebuttal: Theorem 7 is local and sufficient; it neither classifies all remaining orientations nor supplies law-preserving transformations, cardinality, or parameter uniqueness.

seed_details.title: Sharp degree-four completeness of the log-PGF
seed_details.anchor_opened: Introduction, Remark 1, Theorems 1, 3, 5--7, the path-cumulant construction around equations (8)--(10), the reversal example, and Conclusion were read in the AAAI paper and author preprint.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Qiao et al. let the discriminating cumulant order depend on path multiplicity; the first changed step is to quotient branching genealogies by repeated observed labels and prove that degree-four local certificates suffice regardless of the number of directed paths.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Qiao et al. because their arbitrary-order cumulants already encode every directed path.
seed_details.rebuttal: Encoding at unbounded order does not imply a graph-independent cutoff, and the strict triangle witness makes minimality a separate theorem.

seed_details.title: Finite-sample outward inversion for the full strict-model fiber
seed_details.anchor_opened: The empirical PGF discussion, Algorithm 1, the bootstrap rank tests, the two real-data analyses, and the Conclusion limitation on sample-efficient PGF estimation were read together with the population PGF theorems.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is to replace a thresholded point decoder by a joint confidence region for finitely many bounded count-cell probabilities and then propagate the entire region through a set-valued inverse.
seed_details.method_thread: strieder2021confidence was opened at its test-inversion construction and Theorem 1; wang2026confidence was opened at its ordering-set coverage statement and relation-envelope post-processing.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from standard Hoeffding bounds because every required cell indicator is bounded.
seed_details.rebuttal: Coordinate concentration is routine, but denominator-safe rational mapping, outward inversion over all strict representations, and simultaneous coverage of a non-singleton population fiber are not supplied by concentration alone.

seed_details.title: Reverse-topological rational inverse on a fixed DAG
seed_details.anchor_opened: The recursive PGF representation in Theorems 1--2, its Appendix A proof, and the local adjacency construction were read.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first new step is to isolate singleton failure probabilities and solve every edge coefficient and innovation rate in reverse topological order from singleton and pair log-PGF coefficients.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate algebra from the pair coefficient displayed by Xiang et al.
seed_details.rebuttal: The recursion is short once found, but the published paper does not state global parameter injectivity or use the inverse to certify one parameter point on every graph in a population fiber.

seed_details.title: Exact compelled-edge and ambiguity certificates
seed_details.anchor_opened: Remark 1 and the bivariate reverse representation, Theorems 6--7, their path-count construction, and the football-event conclusion were read.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first new step is to turn the two-node reversal into a source-edge transformation inside an arbitrary DAG and prove that a sequence of such transformations reaches every and only every free-tree root choice.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from the bivariate reversal formula by applying it edge by edge.
seed_details.rebuttal: An arbitrary edge reversal can create a cycle or alter shared descendants; the source and sole-parent hypotheses, complete-PGF identity, and exhaustion of all ambiguities require a global proof.

seed_details.title: Boundary-stratified fibers with zero or deterministic thinning
seed_details.anchor_opened: Definition 1, Remark 1, the cumulant-path theorems, and the Appendix reversal construction were read with attention to the allowed coefficient boundary.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is the positivity argument: when a failure probability vanishes or an innovation rate is zero, monomial absence no longer certifies graphical absence and the decoder acquires singular strata.
seed_details.target_method_search: A focused search pairing PB-SCM with boundary thinning, deterministic thinning, zero innovation, and observational equivalence returned only the two 2024 PB-SCM papers and no stratified fiber theorem.
seed_details.red_team: A routine closure of the strict result by continuity.
seed_details.rebuttal: Continuity does not preserve support certificates or parameter injectivity at the faces, so a correct result would require a new stratified equivalence theory.

seed_details.title: Exact partial-to-full identification frontier for mixed innovation families
seed_details.anchor_opened: Introduction, Proposition 13, Theorem 14, their Appendix proofs, the exceptional-Poisson argument, and Conclusion were read in the arXiv HTML.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Gao et al. assume every nonsink innovation is non-Poisson; the first changed step is to characterize which connected all-Poisson regions retain source-reversal ambiguity when only a subset of nonsinks has non-Poisson innovations.
seed_details.target_method_search: A focused search pairing mixed Poisson and non-Poisson innovations with PB-SCM identifiability found Gao et al. but no necessary-and-sufficient mixed-family frontier.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Gao et al. by recursively removing every identifiable non-Poisson sink.
seed_details.rebuttal: The recursive sink theorem is sufficient under a universal nonsink condition and does not classify residual equivalences when Poisson and non-Poisson nodes coexist.
seed_details.disposition: dropped because the destination model dilutes the strict all-Poisson kernel

seed_details.title: Polynomial-delay exact enumeration of coefficient-compatible graphs
seed_details.anchor_opened: Introduction, the test-inversion setup, Theorem 1 and its proof, the split-likelihood construction, and Conclusion were read in the UAI paper.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is computational: replace inversion over two smooth linear-SEM models by exact feasibility over finitely many rational PB-SCM coefficient maps, exploiting the source-forest quotient instead of generic real quantifier elimination.
seed_details.target_method_search: Searches pairing PB-SCM confidence sets with finite-sample graph inversion returned no exact or polynomial-delay method.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate by enumerating all DAGs and applying quantifier elimination.
seed_details.rebuttal: Termination by generic enumeration is not a polynomial-delay certificate and does not exploit the new fiber geometry; the efficient exact algorithm remains genuinely open.

seed_details.title: Feedback Poisson-branching distribution equivalence
seed_details.anchor_opened: Introduction, the acyclic sink-recursion proof, and Conclusion were read; the Conclusion explicitly leaves feedback systems open.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is existence and factorization: topological recursion disappears under feedback, so the cluster PGF must be replaced by a subcritical branching fixed point before equivalence can be classified.
seed_details.target_method_search: A focused search pairing cyclic or feedback PB-SCM with identifiability returned no feedback PB-SCM fiber result.
seed_details.red_team: A direct cyclic extension of the acyclic PGF recursion.
seed_details.rebuttal: Cycles require subcriticality, fixed-point uniqueness, and a new equivalence algebra; none follows from the DAG recursion.

literature_map.chosen_kernel: The strict all-Poisson PB-SCM fiber is the selected kernel. Xiang et al. supply the recursive PGF and complete local parent-pair signatures; Qiao et al. supply path-cumulant intuition and the two-node reversal; Ghassami et al. supply the distinction between one-law fibers and graph-level distribution equivalence; Gao et al. confirm that the all-Poisson case is exceptional but change the thinning or innovation family to obtain full identification.
candidate_S1_threads: Xiang et al., Theorems 1--2 and Proposition 1: recursive PGF factors and monomials encode branching paths.
Xiang et al., Theorems 4--7: singleton, pair, triangle, and collider tests orient arrows entering locally detected multi-parent vertices, but no global converse is stated.
Qiao et al., Remark 1 and Appendix B: every strict two-node edge has an explicit reverse representation.

Ghassami et al., Definition 3 and Theorem 1: full distribution-set equivalence is classified through explicit algebraic transformations in linear Gaussian graphs, whereas the present target is the fiber of one PB-SCM law.
candidate_S2_threads: Qiao et al., Theorems 3, 5--7: the discriminating cumulant order is tied to directed-path multiplicity.
Xiang et al., Theorem 2 and Proposition 1: the complete PGF contains monomials whose coordinate multiplicities can grow with overlapping paths.
Nakamura and Perez-Abreu: empirical PGF methods motivate finite-dimensional estimation once a universal coefficient cutoff is available.
candidate_S3_threads: Xiang et al., Algorithm 1 and Conclusion: bootstrap rank tests output a learned partially directed graph and sample-efficient PGF estimation remains open.
Strieder et al., Theorem 1: test inversion accounts jointly for structural and numerical uncertainty in restricted linear models.
Wang, Kolar, and Drton, equation (1.2) and Section 4.3: nonrejected causal orderings are post-processed into relation envelopes, with emptiness interpreted as model criticism.
Nakamura and Perez-Abreu: empirical PGFs are averages of bounded transforms, while the present construction uses bounded count-cell indicators and a rational log-series map.
literature_map.occupation_check: Focused searches through September 11, 2026 found no arbitrary-DAG source-forest converse, no universal sharp degree-four truncation theorem, and no simultaneous finite-sample confidence set covering the entire unrestricted strict PB-SCM fiber. Gao et al. call the strict all-Poisson DAG only partially identifiable and obtain full identification by changing the model rather than characterizing that fiber. The latent-confounded Qiao et al. paper addresses local three-variable monomial equivalence in a different model.
literature_map.writing_exemplar_used: Xiang et al. is used for the event-count motivation, the transition from branching semantics to PGF geometry, and the football and shopping applications.
literature_map.method_exemplars_used: The recursive PGF and local monomial arguments of Xiang et al., the bivariate reversal algebra of Qiao et al., the distribution-versus-Markov-equivalence distinction of Ghassami et al., and the set-inversion logic of Strieder et al. and Wang et al. are adapted.

novelty_justification: The closest published results are Xiang et al. (2024) and Qiao et al. (2024). Xiang et al. identify the skeleton and give sufficient local PGF criteria, including every arrow whose head has another parent, but do not characterize all globally compatible DAGs, all parameter points, or the residual ambiguity. Qiao et al. prove only path-based sufficient orientation criteria and a bivariate reverse representation. The precise advance is an if-and-only-if one-law fiber theorem: after the locally compelled incoming arrows are deleted, the residual graph is a forest, anchored roots are forced, free components reroot independently, every rerooting is realized by a positive complete-PGF-preserving transformation, and no other representation exists. A reverse-topological rational decoder yields one parameter point per compatible DAG. Degree-four coefficients then become a universal and minimal complete signature, and their bounded-cell representation permits finite-sample outer coverage of the full fiber. Searches also checked Gao et al. (2026), who obtain full identification only after changing thinning or nonsink innovation laws, and found no closer theorem subsuming this strict all-Poisson kernel.
